0.title: Opening Our Lives and Our Homes
0.overview:
We live in an age of many connections and few friends. People have hundreds of online contacts but often no one they can call at two in the morning. Loneliness has become widespread, affecting the young and the old, the single and the married. Meanwhile, homes have become private retreats, and the old habit of having people round for a meal has faded in many places.

Scripture has a great deal to say about both friendship and hospitality. God made us for relationship. Jesus called his disciples friends. The early church met in homes and broke bread together. And hospitality, literally the love of strangers, is a command for every Christian, not just a gift for some.

This study looks at why we were made for friendship, what makes a true friend, how to choose friends wisely, why hospitality matters and how God's welcome to us shapes our welcome to others.

Five units: (1) Made for Friendship; (2) Marks of a True Friend; (3) Choosing Friends Wisely; (4) The Ministry of Hospitality; (5) Welcomed by God, Welcoming Others.

1.title: Made for Friendship
1.overview:
Not good to be alone. In a world that God called good, one thing was not good: It is not good that the man should be alone (Gen 2:18). God's answer was marriage, but the principle reaches wider. Human beings were made for relationship. We reflect a God who is himself a fellowship of love, Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

Two are better than one. Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow. But woe to him who is alone when he falls and has not another to lift him up! (Eccl 4:9-10). Friends help in work, lift us when we fall, warm us when we are cold and defend us when we are attacked. A threefold cord is not quickly broken (Eccl 4:12).

A friend closer than a brother. A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother (Prov 18:24). Many acquaintances are not the same as true friends. One loyal friend is worth more than a crowd of shallow connections.

Jesus calls us friends. On the night before his death, Jesus said to his disciples, No longer do I call you servants, for the servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you (John 15:15). The Lord of glory calls his followers friends. He shares his heart with them. And he showed the greatest friendship of all: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends (John 15:13).

Friendship with God. Abraham was called a friend of God (Jas 2:23). The LORD spoke with Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend (Exod 33:11). Through Christ, every believer is brought into friendship with God. This is the deepest friendship there is, and it shapes all others.
1.theology:
Friendship and the church: The church is a family of brothers and sisters, and deep friendships should grow within it. But friendship is particular; we cannot be close friends with everyone. Jesus loved all his disciples, but had an inner circle of three, and one called the disciple whom Jesus loved (John 13:23).

Friendship and marriage: Marriage at its best includes deep friendship. This is my beloved and this is my friend (Song 5:16). But married people also need other friends; no spouse can meet every relational need.

Friendship across generations: Scripture values friendships between older and younger believers: Naomi and Ruth, Paul and Timothy, Elijah and Elisha. These friendships pass on wisdom and faith.
1.examples:
Then: In his final letter, written from prison, Paul mentioned many friends by name. He asked Timothy to come quickly, and to bring Mark and his cloak. Luke alone is with me (2 Tim 4:11). The great apostle needed friends, and he was not ashamed to say so.

Now: A man in his fifties realises that, apart from his wife, he has no close friends. His life has been work and family. He asks two men from church to meet for breakfast once a month. At first it feels awkward. Five years later, they are the first people he calls in a crisis.

A simple test: Who would you call at two in the morning if you were in trouble? Who would call you?

verseByVerse.quote: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow. But woe to him who is alone when he falls and has not another to lift him up! Again, if two lie together, they keep warm, but how can one keep warm alone? And though a man might prevail against one who is alone, two will withstand him—a threefold cord is not quickly broken. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Preacher has just described a lonely man who works endlessly with no one to share it with (Eccl 4:8). Then he praises companionship. Two can work better, lift each other up, keep warm and defend themselves. A third strand makes the cord stronger still. Life is meant to be shared.

verseByVerse.quote: "This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. No longer do I call you servants, for the servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus commands his disciples to love one another as he has loved them. The greatest love is to lay down one's life for friends, which he was about to do. Then he calls them friends, not servants, because he has made known to them everything from the Father. Friendship with Jesus is the foundation of Christian friendship.

verseByVerse.quote: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This proverb contrasts many companions with one true friend. Superficial connections can leave us ruined when trouble comes. But a true friend sticks closer than a brother. Quality matters more than quantity in friendship.

verseByVerse.quote: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far off from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp. Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise up, and each would stand at his tent door, and watch Moses until he had gone into the tent. When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the LORD would speak with Moses. And when all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, all the people would rise up and worship, each at his tent door. Thus the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. When Moses turned again into the camp, his assistant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Moses pitched the tent of meeting outside the camp, and God's presence came down in the pillar of cloud. The LORD spoke with Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. In the middle of a story of Israel's rebellion, here is a picture of intimate friendship with God.

1.reflection:
Why do you think God said it is "not good" to be alone?

Who are your closest friends? How did those friendships begin?

What does it mean to you that Jesus calls his followers friends?

Is there someone in your church who seems lonely? How could you reach out?

2.title: Marks of a True Friend
2.overview:
Scripture paints a clear picture of what true friendship looks like.

Loyalty. A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity (Prov 17:17). True friends stay in hard times. When Ruth's mother-in-law Naomi was bereaved and bitter, Ruth refused to leave her: For where you go I will go, and where you lodge I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God (Ruth 1:16).

Covenant love. Jonathan, son of King Saul, loved David as his own soul (1 Sam 18:1). He gave David his robe and armour, defended him before his father and risked his life to protect him. Their friendship was sealed by a covenant. Jonathan rejoiced in David's future even though it meant he would never be king.

Honesty. Faithful are the wounds of a friend (Prov 27:6). A true friend tells us the truth, even when it hurts. Flatterers tell us what we want to hear; friends tell us what we need to hear.

Counsel. Oil and perfume make the heart glad, and the sweetness of a friend comes from his earnest counsel (Prov 27:9). Friends help us think, decide and see what we cannot see alone.

Sharpening. Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another (Prov 27:17). Good friends make each other better. They challenge, encourage and stretch one another in faith and character.

Presence in suffering. When Job lost everything, his three friends came and sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his suffering was very great (Job 2:13). Their silence was their best ministry. Later, when they started explaining his suffering, they went wrong.

Forgiveness. Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but he who repeats a matter separates close friends (Prov 17:9). Lasting friendships require overlooking small offences and forgiving larger ones.
2.theology:
Christ the true friend: Every mark of friendship is perfectly found in Christ. He is loyal (he never leaves us), honest (he tells us the truth), wise in counsel, present in suffering and forgiving. He laid down his life for his friends. Christian friendship reflects his friendship.

Friendship and sacrifice: Real friendship costs time, effort, inconvenience and sometimes reputation. Jonathan risked his father's anger. Ruth gave up her homeland. True friends give themselves.

Same-sex friendship: Deep friendships between men and between women are good and biblical. Our culture often sexualises close friendships or regards them with suspicion. Scripture honours them.
2.examples:
Then: When David and Jonathan parted for the last time, knowing Saul was hunting David, they kissed one another and wept with one another, David weeping the most (1 Sam 20:41). Later, when Jonathan died in battle, David lamented, very pleasant have you been to me (2 Sam 1:26).

Now: Two women became friends at a church toddler group twenty years ago. They have since walked together through a divorce, a cancer diagnosis, rebellious teenagers and the death of parents. They have also told each other hard truths. Each says the other is God's gift to her.

A simple test: Which of these marks of friendship are you strongest in? Which do you need to grow in?

verseByVerse.quote: As soon as he had finished speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. And Saul took him that day and would not let him return to his father's house. Then Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as his own soul. And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to David, and his armor, and even his sword and his bow and his belt. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jonathan's soul was knit to David's soul. He made a covenant with him and gave him his own robe, armour, sword, bow and belt. Jonathan was the king's son and heir, yet he gave David the symbols of his own position. True friendship is generous and humble.

verseByVerse.quote: And she said, "See, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods; return after your sister-in-law." But Ruth said, "Do not urge me to leave you or to return from following you. For where you go I will go, and where you lodge I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God. Where you die I will die, and there will I be buried. May the LORD do so to me and more also if anything but death parts me from you." And when Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she said no more. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Naomi urged Ruth to go back home. Ruth refused. Her words are among the most moving expressions of loyalty in literature. She bound herself to Naomi's people, Naomi's God and even Naomi's grave. Friendship became faith, as Ruth joined the people of the LORD.

verseByVerse.quote: Better is open rebuke than hidden love. Faithful are the wounds of a friend; profuse are the kisses of an enemy. One who is full loathes honey, but to one who is hungry everything bitter is sweet. Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home. Oil and perfume make the heart glad, and the sweetness of a friend comes from his earnest counsel. Do not forsake your friend and your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house in the day of your calamity. Better is a neighbor who is near than a brother who is far away. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This cluster of proverbs describes friendship. Open rebuke is better than hidden love. A friend's wounds are faithful. A friend's counsel is sweet. And do not forsake your friend or your father's friend. Long-standing friendships across generations are precious.

verseByVerse.quote: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that had come upon him, they came each from his own place, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They made an appointment together to come to show him sympathy and comfort him. And when they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him. And they raised their voices and wept, and they tore their robes and sprinkled dust on their heads toward heaven. And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his suffering was very great. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Job's three friends heard about his suffering and came to comfort him. They wept, tore their robes and sat with him in silence for seven days. This was compassion at its best. Their mistake came later, when they tried to explain. Sometimes the best thing a friend can do is simply be there.

2.reflection:
Which mark of a true friend means most to you? Why?

Read 1 Samuel 18-20. What made the friendship of David and Jonathan so remarkable?

Have you ever been wounded faithfully by a friend? What did it do for you?

How can you be a better friend to someone this month?

3.title: Choosing Friends Wisely
3.overview:
Friends shape us more than we realise. Scripture urges wisdom in choosing them.

We become like our friends. Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools will suffer harm (Prov 13:20). Over time, we absorb the values, habits and attitudes of those we spend time with. Do not be deceived: "Bad company ruins good morals." (1 Cor 15:33).

Avoid the angry and the gossip. Make no friendship with a man given to anger, nor go with a wrathful man, lest you learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare (Prov 22:24-25). A dishonest man spreads strife, and a whisperer separates close friends (Prov 16:28). Some people's company is spiritually dangerous.

The way of the wicked. Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of scoffers (Ps 1:1). Notice the progression: walking, standing, sitting. Influence often grows gradually.

Friends with unbelievers. This does not mean Christians should have no unbelieving friends. Jesus was called a friend of tax collectors and sinners (Matt 11:19). Christians should love, befriend and serve unbelievers. But our closest friends, the ones who shape our decisions and values, should share our faith. A good test: in this friendship, who is influencing whom?

Be the friend you seek. Rather than only looking for good friends, we should aim to be good friends: loyal, honest, encouraging and godly.

When friendships fail. Even good friendships can be broken by sin, misunderstanding or distance. David's close friend Ahithophel betrayed him (2 Sam 15:31; Ps 55:12-14). Jesus was betrayed by Judas, one of the twelve. Betrayal is deeply painful. Where possible, seek reconciliation. Where not, entrust it to God.
3.theology:
Wisdom literature: Proverbs is full of advice about friendship because friendship is one of the main ways wisdom or folly is passed on. Choosing friends is a moral decision.

Influence and witness: Christians are called to be salt and light among unbelievers. But salt must not lose its saltiness. The question is whether we are influencing our friends toward Christ, or they are influencing us away from him.

Christ's friendship with sinners: Jesus befriended sinners without becoming like them. His holiness was not threatened by their company; rather, they were changed by his. This is the model for Christian friendship with unbelievers.
3.examples:
Then: Rehoboam rejected the advice of the older men who had served his father and listened to the young men who had grown up with him (1 Kgs 12:8). His friends gave him foolish advice, and he lost most of his kingdom.

Now: A teenager starts spending time with a new group of friends who mock church and drink heavily. Over a few months, his parents notice changes in his attitude. A youth leader befriends him, invites him to a Christian camp and helps him find friends who share his faith. His other friendships continue, but they no longer shape him most.

A simple test: Who are the three people who influence you most? Are they leading you toward Christ or away from him?

verseByVerse.quote: Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools will suffer harm. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This simple proverb states a powerful principle. Walk with the wise and you become wise. Keep company with fools and you will suffer. We cannot avoid being shaped by those around us, so we must choose carefully.

verseByVerse.quote: Make no friendship with a man given to anger, nor go with a wrathful man, lest you learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Proverbs warns against befriending a hot-tempered person. The reason is not that such people are beyond love, but that their ways are contagious. We may learn their habits and become trapped. Some friendships require caution.

verseByVerse.quote: Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of scoffers; but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night. He is like a tree planted by streams of water that yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither. In all that he does, he prospers. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The blessed person avoids the counsel, path and seat of the wicked, and delights in God's law instead. He is like a tree planted by streams of water, fruitful and flourishing. Our companions and our meditations together shape what kind of person we become.

verseByVerse.quote: For it is not an enemy who taunts me— then I could bear it; it is not an adversary who deals insolently with me— then I could hide from him. But it is you, a man, my equal, my companion, my familiar friend. We used to take sweet counsel together; within God's house we walked in the throng. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David describes the pain of betrayal by a close friend. An enemy's insults he could bear. But it was his companion, his familiar friend, with whom he had walked to God's house. Betrayal by a friend is one of the deepest wounds. David brought it to God.

3.reflection:
Who are the people who most influence you? How are they shaping you?

How can Christians be friends with unbelievers without being drawn away from Christ?

Have you experienced betrayal by a friend? How did you respond?

What kind of friend are you to others?

4.title: The Ministry of Hospitality
4.overview:
A command for all. Contribute to the needs of the saints and seek to show hospitality (Rom 12:13). Show hospitality to one another without grumbling (1 Pet 4:9). Hospitality is not optional or only for those with large homes or a gift for cooking. It is a command for every Christian, and a requirement for church leaders (1 Tim 3:2).

Love of strangers. The New Testament word for hospitality combines "love" and "stranger." It means welcoming not only friends but those outside our usual circle. Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares (Heb 13:2). This recalls Abraham, who ran to welcome three travellers and prepared a meal for them, perhaps not knowing at first that the LORD himself was among them (Gen 18:1-8).

Not for repayment. Jesus told a host, When you give a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you be repaid. But when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind, and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you (Luke 14:12-14). Christian hospitality is not social networking. It reaches those who cannot return the favour.

Without grumbling. Peter's phrase is realistic. Hospitality can be inconvenient, tiring and costly. Guests can be difficult. But we are to open our homes cheerfully, as an act of love.

Simple is fine. Hospitality does not require a perfect house or an elaborate meal. It means opening our lives: a cup of tea, soup and bread, a seat at the family table. The point is welcome, not impressing guests.

The early church. The first Christians met in their homes and received their food with glad and generous hearts (Acts 2:46). Homes were the centres of Christian community and mission. Lydia opened her home to Paul and his companions (Acts 16:15). Priscilla and Aquila hosted a church in their house (1 Cor 16:19).
4.theology:
Hospitality and mission: Many people who would never come to a church will come to a home for a meal. Hospitality is one of the most natural and effective ways of sharing life and faith with unbelieving neighbours.

Hospitality and the gospel: When we welcome others, we reflect God's welcome to us. We were strangers and enemies, and God invited us to his table. Hospitality is a living picture of the gospel.

Wisdom and safety: Hospitality should be practised with wisdom. Families should consider the safety of children, and churches should help members discern when and how to welcome those they do not know.
4.examples:
Then: A wealthy woman in Shunem noticed the prophet Elisha passing through. She said to her husband, Let us make a small room on the roof with walls and put there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp (2 Kgs 4:10). Her hospitality led to God's blessing on her family.

Now: A busy family decides to keep one Sunday lunch a month for inviting people from church they do not know well, especially newcomers, international students and those living alone. The food is simple and the house is often messy. Over the years, dozens of people say those lunches made them feel they belonged.

A simple test: When did you last have someone in your home who could not repay you?

verseByVerse.quote: Let love be genuine. Abhor what is evil; hold fast to what is good. Love one another with brotherly affection. Outdo one another in showing honor. Do not be slothful in zeal, be fervent in spirit, serve the Lord. Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, be constant in prayer. Contribute to the needs of the saints and seek to show hospitality. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul describes genuine love: hating evil, holding fast to good, affection for one another, outdoing one another in showing honour, zeal in serving the Lord. And he includes practical care: contributing to the needs of the saints and seeking to show hospitality. The word "seek" suggests active pursuit, not waiting for opportunities to arrive.

verseByVerse.quote: Let brotherly love continue. Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares. Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you also are in the body. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The writer urges brotherly love, hospitality to strangers and care for prisoners and the mistreated. Hospitality is linked with entertaining angels without knowing it, as Abraham did. We never know whom God is sending to our door.

verseByVerse.quote: He said also to the man who had invited him, "When you give a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you be repaid. But when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind, and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the just." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus tells his host to invite those who cannot repay: the poor, crippled, lame and blind. The reward will come at the resurrection of the just. Christian hospitality reflects the kingdom, where the least are honoured guests at God's table.

verseByVerse.quote: Above all, keep loving one another earnestly, since love covers a multitude of sins. Show hospitality to one another without grumbling. As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace: whoever speaks, as one who speaks oracles of God; whoever serves, as one who serves by the strength that God supplies—in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter puts hospitality between love and gifts. Love covers many sins; hospitality should be shown without grumbling; gifts should be used to serve one another. Hospitality is a practical form of love and a way of stewarding God's grace.

4.reflection:
What keeps you from practising hospitality more? How could you overcome it?

Read Luke 14:12-14. Who could you invite who cannot repay you?

How can simple hospitality be a way of sharing the gospel?

Plan one act of hospitality for the next month.

5.title: Welcomed by God, Welcoming Others
5.overview:
God welcomes us. The deepest reason for Christian hospitality is that God has welcomed us. Therefore welcome one another as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God (Rom 15:7). We were strangers and enemies, outside the household of God. In Christ we have been brought near, made members of his family and invited to his table (Eph 2:12-19).

Jesus welcomed sinners. The religious leaders complained, This man receives sinners and eats with them (Luke 15:2). Jesus ate with tax collectors, invited himself to Zacchaeus's house and fed thousands on a hillside. His table was open to the outcast. Christian hospitality follows his example.

Welcoming the foreigner. In the Old Testament, God commanded Israel to welcome the sojourner: You shall treat the stranger who sojourns with you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt (Lev 19:34). Israel's own history of being foreigners was to make them compassionate. Christians, once spiritual strangers, should likewise show kindness to those far from home.

Serving Christ in his people. Jesus said that on the last day the King will say, I was a stranger and you welcomed me (Matt 25:35). The righteous will ask when they did this, and he will answer, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me (Matt 25:40). Jesus identifies with his brothers, his needy followers. Welcoming them is welcoming him. And the wider law of love, shown in the Good Samaritan, extends kindness to every neighbour in need.

The great banquet. All hospitality now points forward to the feast to come. Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9). Every meal shared in Christ's name is a foretaste of that table, where people from every nation will sit together with the Lord who welcomed them.
5.theology:
Matthew 25 and its scope: Some read the least of these my brothers as referring to all poor people. Elsewhere in Matthew, Jesus' "brothers" are his disciples (Matt 12:49-50; 28:10). The passage most naturally speaks of how the world treats Christ's needy followers. But the Bible's wider teaching, such as the Good Samaritan, calls Christians to show mercy to all.

Hospitality and church unity: Paul's command to welcome one another in Romans 15 was given to a church divided between Jewish and Gentile believers. Hospitality across cultural, social and generational lines is a powerful sign of the gospel's reconciling power.

Not earning salvation: Welcoming others does not earn God's welcome. It flows from it. Those who have been welcomed become welcoming.
5.examples:
Then: Jesus saw Zacchaeus, a despised tax collector, in a tree and said, Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today (Luke 19:5). The crowd grumbled. But Zacchaeus received Jesus joyfully, and salvation came to his house. Jesus' welcome changed his life.

Now: A church in a city with many international students starts a Friday evening meal in members' homes. Students from many countries come, some far from family for the first time. Over the years, friendships form, Bible studies begin and several students come to faith. Others return home with fond memories of Christians who welcomed them.

A simple test: Who in your community is a stranger, far from home or on the margins? How could you welcome them?

verseByVerse.quote: May the God of endurance and encouragement grant you to live in such harmony with one another, in accord with Christ Jesus, that together you may with one voice glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore welcome one another as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul prays for unity among believers with different convictions, so that they might glorify God together with one voice. Then he commands: welcome one another as Christ welcomed you. Christ's welcome is the pattern and the motive. And the goal is the glory of God.

verseByVerse.quote: "When a stranger sojourns with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong. You shall treat the stranger who sojourns with you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Israel was to treat the foreigner as a native-born citizen and love him as themselves. The reason was their own history: they had been strangers in Egypt. God's people remember where they came from, and that memory makes them merciful.

verseByVerse.quote: He entered Jericho and was passing through. And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector and was rich. And he was seeking to see who Jesus was, but on account of the crowd he could not, because he was small in stature. So he ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was about to pass that way. And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today." So he hurried and came down and received him joyfully. And when they saw it, they all grumbled, "He has gone in to be the guest of a man who is a sinner." And Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor. And if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold." And Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, since he also is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Zacchaeus was rich and despised. Jesus invited himself to his house. The welcome changed Zacchaeus: he gave half his goods to the poor and repaid fourfold anyone he had cheated. Jesus declared that salvation had come to his house, because the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.

verseByVerse.quote: Then the King will say to those on his right, 'Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me, I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to me.' Then the righteous will answer him, saying, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you? And when did we see you sick or in prison and visit you?' And the King will answer them, 'Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.' (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The King welcomes the righteous into the kingdom prepared for them. He commends them for feeding, clothing, welcoming and visiting him. They are surprised. He explains that what they did for the least of his brothers, they did for him. Love for Christ's people is love for Christ.

5.reflection:
